prompt:
Pixel-art sprite sheet, single image, fully transparent background.

SUBJECT: the undead zombie basketball player in the attached reference image.
Match that character exactly: sickly grey-green skin, ragged mid-brown hair,
sunken eyes with small pale pupils, a lipless grin showing the teeth, dark
rotted patches on the arms and legs, a torn and ragged blue sleeveless
basketball jersey with a yellow number 13, torn blue shorts with white and
yellow trim, white high-top sneakers with blue and yellow flashes over white
socks. Identical colours, identical proportions, identical build and identical
height as the reference, in every frame.

LAYOUT: one horizontal row of 5 frames of equal width, evenly spaced. No
borders, no frame numbers, no labels, no background, no drop shadows.

POSE GUIDE: TWO images are attached, and they do different jobs.

The COLOUR image of the character is the only authority on WHO HE IS. His
colours, his proportions, his build, his height, his face, his kit and the
drawing style all come from that image and from the SUBJECT above, and nothing
below changes any of them.

The other image is a POSE GUIDE: a plain black stick figure on a white
background, five figures standing in a row on one ground line, in the same
left-to-right order as the FRAMES listed below. The Nth figure in the pose
guide is the pose for the Nth frame. Take the GEOMETRY from it and only the
geometry: where each foot stands on the ground line, how deeply the knees are
bent, how far the shoulder line tilts, how far his body leans to one side, and
exactly where each elbow and each hand is. Where the words below and the pose
guide describe the same thing, they agree; the pose guide is the exact version
of it.

THE HANDS ON THE POSE GUIDE are both OPEN, with the palm facing the viewer: the
broad rectangle is the palm, the four lines off its end are the fingers spread
apart, and the short line off its side is the thumb. The hand on the VIEWER'S
RIGHT is raised beside his head, the wrist level with the top of it, fingers
pointing up at the ceiling. The hand on the VIEWER'S LEFT is held low and wide,
out beside his thigh, fingers pointing out and down. Each is ONE drawing, moved
from frame to frame with his body.

THE SHORT LINES ON THE POSE GUIDE'S HEAD are his hair sticking out at rest.
Draw HIS OWN ragged hair that way. The lines are a direction, not hair.

Draw the character from the colour reference standing in those positions. The
pose guide is an instruction, not artwork: its thin flat lines, its joint dots,
its white background, its blank circular head and its missing face are NOT part
of the drawing and must not appear anywhere in it.

CAMERA: locked off. Identical distance and eye level in every frame. The
character must be exactly the same height in every frame, and the same height
as in the reference image — do not zoom, crop, recompose or rescale between
frames. All frames share one ground line: the soles of the feet touch the same
horizontal line in every frame.

VIEW: front view, facing the viewer, squared to camera, in a wide low defensive
stance: knees bent, feet planted well wider than his shoulders, weight on the
balls of his feet. He does NOT have the ball and is not dribbling.

CRITICAL: this is a basketball DEFENDER'S stance, and the two hands do
DIFFERENT jobs. They are held the same way in all four frames.

THE HAND NEARER THE RIGHT EDGE OF THE PICTURE IS RAISED: elbow bent and
pointing out to the side, level with his chest, forearm upright, and the hand
held up beside his head, the wrist level with the top of his head and the
fingers reaching above it, palm open and facing the viewer, fingers spread and
pointing up at the ceiling.

THE HAND NEARER THE LEFT EDGE OF THE PICTURE IS LOW AND WIDE: the arm reaches
OUT SIDEWAYS and down, elbow slightly bent, and the hand is out beyond his hip
at the height of his thigh, well clear of his leg, palm open and facing the
viewer, fingers spread and pointing out and down.

NEITHER ARM IS STRETCHED STRAIGHT OUT IN FRONT OF HIM toward the viewer, and
neither is held at shoulder height reaching forward. Both elbows point OUT TO
THE SIDES, so each whole arm shows against the background, clear of his body.
Neither hand reaches down toward the floor — nothing about this pose suggests
dribbling.

HIS FEET ARE ONE DRAWING REPEATED IN ALL FOUR FRAMES: both shoes in the same
place on the floor, the same wide distance apart, at the same angle. He moves
by BENDING AND STRAIGHTENING HIS KNEES and shifting his weight from one leg to
the other, never by moving his feet.

HIS HEAD sits on top of his spine and his face stays turned to the viewer,
alert, eyes on the viewer as if the viewer were the player he is guarding.

FRAMES, left to right:
1. CALIBRATION POSE: standing straight upright, feet shoulder-width apart, arms
   hanging relaxed at his sides, facing the viewer, in the plain neutral
   standing pose from the reference image. This exact pose appears as the first
   frame of every sheet in this set and must be drawn identically every time.
2. SET LEFT, one of his two lowest frames: knees bent deepest, his weight
   shifted onto the leg nearer the LEFT EDGE of the picture, his hips and
   shoulders leaning a little toward that edge and the shoulder line tilted
   down on that side. Both hands exactly as described, moved with his body.
3. UP, weight back in the middle: knees straightened a little so he stands a
   touch taller, shoulders and hips level, still a wide low stance. Both hands
   exactly as described, a little higher with his body.
4. SET RIGHT, the mirror of SET LEFT in the body only: knees bent deepest, his
   weight shifted onto the leg nearer the RIGHT EDGE of the picture, his hips
   and shoulders leaning a little toward that edge and the shoulder line tilted
   down on that side. The hands do NOT swap: the raised hand is still the one
   nearer the right edge.
5. UP again, the same drawing as the first UP frame: weight back in the middle,
   shoulders and hips level, a touch taller.

This row is a seamless loop: frame 5 must flow back into frame 2 with no jump.

The difference between the frames is the whole animation: SET LEFT and SET
RIGHT are clearly lower than the two UP frames, and lean opposite ways. His
arms and hands keep one shape throughout, carried up, down and sideways with
his body.

STYLE: VGA-era 256-colour DOS-game pixel art, drawn pixel by pixel — NOT a
modern illustration with a pixel filter over it. The limits below are the look;
keep all of them: - At most THREE tones per material: a base, one darker
shadow, one lighter highlight. Hard edges between the tones. - NO gradients, NO
soft or airbrushed shading, NO glow, NO bloom, and NO anti-aliasing anywhere —
not on the outline, not between tones, not around the silhouette. - Where a
tone change needs softening, use visible ORDERED DITHER — a checkerboard of the
two tones. Dither, never blend. - Chunky square pixels on one consistent grid,
plainly visible at full size. - A bold dark outline around the silhouette and
around the major forms inside it. The background must be fully transparent
(alpha 0) with no haze, glow or soft fringe around the silhouette. Output a
wide landscape image.

The character is NOT holding a basketball in any frame and is NOT dribbling —
the ball is drawn separately by the game and he does not have it.
